rubric.scale: 0-10 per component; 5 is globally neutral; scores map linearly to score units as z = (score - 5) / 2. Authored scores are editorial judgments informed by public data and the geostrategic literature (Zeihan et al.); they are deliberately shipped in this file so readers can audit or fork them.
rubric.geo: Geographic security: defensibility of borders, ocean moats vs open plains, strategic depth, exposure to great-power coercion.
rubric.agri: Agricultural potential: arable land per capita, water security, input-import dependence of the food system.
rubric.ener: Energy & resources: domestic energy production vs import dependence, resource endowments relevant to industry.
rubric.trade: Neighborhood & trade resilience: quality/stability of neighbors and market access if long-haul trade degrades; export-dependence penalized, adjacency to large healthy markets rewarded.
rubric.cap: Capital access: depth and openness of domestic capital markets, reserve/safe-haven status, sovereign balance sheet.

notes.geo: Two ocean moats, benign neighbors, unmatched internal waterways.
notes.agri: The Midwest is the planet's largest contiguous prime farmland.
notes.ener: Shale made it a net energy exporter; full-spectrum resource base.
notes.trade: USMCA is a near-self-contained consumption-driven system.
notes.cap: Deepest capital markets and the reserve currency.

notes.geo: Deserts and mountains buffer it; cartel conflict is the internal tax.
notes.agri: Decent but water-stressed in the industrial north.
notes.ener: Oil legacy in decline, underinvested grid.
notes.trade: Land border with the world's biggest consumer market — the single best trade position of any middle-income country.
notes.cap: Improving but shallow; nearshoring is importing capital for it.

notes.geo: Buffered by desert, mountain and ocean, but its sea lanes run through hostile chokepoints.
notes.agri: Arable land per capita is thin and the water table north of the Yangtze is failing.
notes.ener: The largest energy importer in history; seaborne supply lines it cannot convoy.
notes.trade: Export-led model aimed at customers it is antagonizing, via chokepoints it does not control.
notes.cap: Vast but captive savings; capital controls and politicized allocation.

notes.geo: Island moat plus the US alliance; the original defensible archipelago.
notes.trade: Deep blue-water navy and diversified FDI soften raw import exposure.
notes.cap: Enormous domestic savings pool and external asset position.

notes.geo: A peninsula wedged between China, Japan and a nuclear sibling.
notes.agri: Limited arable land, heavy import reliance.
notes.trade: The most export-dependent major economy, with the worst demographic cliff.
notes.cap: Sophisticated markets, strong chaebol balance sheets.

notes.geo: The North European Plain is indefensible in both directions.
notes.ener: Bet on Russian gas and lost; industrial energy costs now structural.
notes.trade: An export machine whose customers (EU, China) are aging faster than it is.
notes.cap: Deep, conservative capital base; the eurozone's anchor.

notes.geo: Alpine wall in the north, but long exposed coastlines.
notes.ener: High import dependence, contested Mediterranean supply.
notes.trade: Mid-tier manufacturing squeezed between Germany and Asia.
notes.cap: Chronic sovereign-debt overhang caps fiscal room.

notes.geo: No natural western border — hence the permanent expansion reflex; depth is its only moat.
notes.agri: A top wheat exporter despite climate limits.
notes.trade: Sanctioned out of premium markets; hostage to discount buyers.
notes.cap: Frozen reserves, expropriation risk, no external capital access.

notes.geo: Himalayan wall and an ocean named after it.
notes.agri: The Ganges basin feeds 1.4bn but monsoon and groundwater risk loom.
notes.ener: Heavy import dependence, though diversified suppliers.
notes.trade: Balanced economy, less export-hostage than East Asia.
notes.cap: Improving depth; still capital-scarce for its scale.

notes.geo: Colonial borders binding 250 ethnicities; internal security is the constraint.
notes.agri: Enormous underused potential in the middle belt.
notes.ener: Major oil and gas producer, chronically underinvested.
notes.trade: Gulf of Guinea access but a rough neighborhood.
notes.cap: Shallow markets, capital flight, naira instability.
